item.title: My political beliefs exist in a completely separate part of me, untouched by…
item.description: My political beliefs exist in a completely separate part of me, untouched by the emotions, affection, and love I carry in my heart. They are deeply personal, and I don’t feel the need to reveal or justify them to anyone. I know what I believe, and I will stand by those convictions when the time calls for it. But when it comes to the people I love, I choose understanding over disagreement, listening over imposing my opinions, and love over ideology. My political convictions may shape how I see the world, but I will never let them dictate how I treat the people who matter to me.

item.title: The Echo and the Erasure: A Search for Meaning in the Age of Consensus
item.description:
The Echo and the Erasure: A Search for Meaning in the Age of Consensus

What is happening to our world? We find ourselves adrift in a sea of borrowed narratives, mistaking the echoes of the crowd for our own original voices. We must pause and ask ourselves a terrifying question: Where do our convictions actually come from? Consider the rigid dichotomy of "for" and "against" that dominates our modern discourse. Who built this binary? More importantly, who benefits from it? When we blindly align ourselves with pre-packaged political campaigns or partisan ideologies, we surrender our individualism. We stop thinking and start merely reciting. As in Orwell’s Animal Farm, the complex truths of the world are reduced to mindless, bleating slogans: “Four legs good, two legs bad.” We are slowly being consumed by a new wave of totalitarianism—one that does not force compliance with a weapon, but manufactures it through the subtle, pervasive pressure of groupthink and media trials.

We must relentlessly confront ourselves with the question of purity—intellectual and spiritual purity. Are we critically examining the causes we champion, or are we passively trusting the ideas of those who are already hopelessly compromised by partisan agendas? To reclaim our minds, we must strip away the noise and locate our authentic selves. As Viktor Frankl discovered in the darkest of human conditions, the last and greatest of human freedoms is the ability to choose one's own attitude, to retain an inner sanctuary of independent thought even when the external world tries to crush it.

Furthermore, we comfort ourselves with the naive belief that history is indestructible—that the truth will inevitably survive. But in this era of relentless media manipulation, we are wrong. We are at a high risk of losing the original truth entirely. We are being pushed toward a sanitized, fabricated "paper history." As Orwell warned in 1984, "He who controls the past controls the future."* If we allow the media to rewrite reality to fit a convenient narrative, we will eventually be forced to live inside a lie, accepting that lie as the absolute truth.

To survive this, we must resist the ease of conformity. We must search for meaning not in the collective outrage of the masses, but in the quiet, rigorous, and often uncomfortable pursuit of our own independent truth.

item.title: If someone asks about the moral ground on which the United States is…
item.description:
If someone asks about the moral ground on which the United States is attacking Iran, here is my perspective.

A large number of Iranians do not enjoy many basic freedoms associated with a free society or free person. The main question has to do with the type of government that people naturally choose. Historically, people do not generally choose to have an autocratic form of government and they are even less likely to choose a rigid theocratic type of government. Once the political authority of a state derives from the teachings of a religion, there is no longer any accountability between the political authority and those governed by the political authority. In addition, political authorities claim to possess some form of divine authority.

In such systems there is an element of danger associated with expressing disagreement. In Iran, for example, those who oppose the current Iranian political regime are regularly imprisoned, silenced, and/or killed. When citizens cannot safely protest, organize politically, and/or express opposition to the government, the normal means for affecting internal change become unavailable. Therefore, it is argued that if people cannot use peaceful measures to reform or replace their government, the regime has effectively shut the door on any possibility of internally transforming itself.

This is often presented as a form of moral justification for calls for foreign assistance/pressure/intervention/operation. The regime of Iran has established such a degree of constriction on the population of Iran that there is virtually no possibility to attempt to oppose or resist the government.

While there is no doubt that the historical record provides support for the fact that international intervention does not usually solve a nation’s internal difficulties, it is also abundantly clear that when countries have entered a country of the international community and decided to act, the end result is often instability and will lead to serious consequences for the people of the country involved. Yet political history also shows moments where the international community chooses to take risks in the belief that change is necessary.

WHEN A GOVERNMENT KILLS ITS OWN CITIZENS FOR DEMANDING FREEDOM, IT LOSES THE MORAL FOUNDATION OF ITS POWER.

Leadership is ultimately measured by its treatment of their own citizens. A country that responds to its citizens through violence does not reflect strength as a leader but is, in fact, a sign of their failure to live up to their responsibility as a nation to the citizens that they would claim to represent.

item.title: A few days ago, I thought it was impossible to fight against City Hall. The…
item.description: A few days ago, I thought it was impossible to fight against City Hall. The old establishment like Congress and UML seemed too strong to defeat. But now it feels different; what once seemed unlikely now even opens the possibility of a two-thirds majority for the RSP. The people of Nepal have done their part for change, now it is up to the leaders to deliver.

item.title: नेपालको जनता सरल छन्।
item.description:
नेपालको जनता सरल छन्।

उनीहरूलाई ठूलो वाचा होइन,

केवल जिम्मेवारी इमान्दारीका साथ पूरा भएको देख्न मन पर्छ।

जब नेता आफ्नो दायित्व निभाउँछन्,

जनताको माया सम्मानमा बदलिन्छ,

सम्मान विश्वासमा बदलिन्छ,

र विश्वास इतिहास बन्छ।

त्यसैले आफ्नो जितलाई कहिल्यै सहज नसम्झनुहोस्।

जनताले दिएको जिम्मेवारी पूरा गर्नुहोस्

जनताको माया सधैं तपाईंको साथमा हुनेछ।
